candidates.title: Kolab: Benchmarking Human-Agent Collaboration in Long-Horizon Workflows
candidates.content: When humans collaborate with AI agents on long-horizon tasks, what happens to the agents' contributions? For solving long-horizon tasks, humans place greater importance on ongoing interaction with AI agents (e.g., revising plans) than on an agent's ability to complete the task in a single attempt. However, most agentic benchmarks have focused more on automation. Strong performance on such benchmarks does not imply effective real-world collaboration. Professional workflows offer a useful setting, as they often involve interdependent steps. To address this gap, we introduce Kolab, a new dataset of 115+ hours of screen recordings of 50 professionals from 40 occupations collaborating with agents on realistic, long-horizon problems. Kolab also contains participants' collaboration and output quality judgments. Our analysis reveals diverse collaboration patterns, highlighting the importance of when and how professionals coordinate with agents. candidates.title: Judging the Justification: Decision Certificate Supervision for Generative Reward Models
candidates.content: Generative reward models (GenRMs) generate natural language rationales to justify preference judgments, yet a correct verdict does not guarantee a sound justification. Existing approaches often rely on reference explanations to supervise rationales, but obtaining such references can be costly and does not necessarily establish whether generated rationales support the resulting verdict. To address these limitations, we propose DeCert, a framework that evaluates the validity and verdict consistency of generated rationales without requiring reference explanations. Crucially, DeCert translates these assessments into preference supervision that accounts for both verdict correctness and justification quality. In particular, when multiple sampled judgments share the same correct verdict, differences in certificate quality enable DeCert to construct rationale preference pairs that distinguish stronger from weaker justifications. Extensive empirical studies across two model families and multiple in- and out-of-distribution benchmarks demonstrate that DeCert consistently outperforms strong generative judge baselines while improving rationale quality. candidates.title: On the Token Collapse Phenomenon in Textual Graph Soft Prompting
candidates.content: Recent methods for injecting graph structure into LLM prompts include graph soft prompting, in which a graph neural network (GNN) learns graph-specific tokens that capture relational information among entities in textual prompts. G-Retriever combines graph soft prompts with a verbalized description of the same graph to strengthen the textual prompt signal. We conduct an in-depth analysis of G-Retriever and uncover a pathological behavior we term token collapse. Across three benchmarks, three graph encoders, two LLM families, and both frozen and LoRA-adapted models, G-Retriever's graph tokens become almost indistinguishable across inputs. We provide evidence that the same failure is inherited by subsequent methods, even with multi-token pooling. Under the standard setup, swapping a token with the dataset mean, a token from another example, or one derived from a corrupted graph produces no resolved answer-level effect in accuracy. Moreover, a learned constant prompt that never accesses the graph matches or surpasses G-Retriever on all three benchmarks. candidates.title: Structural basis for coupled DNA replication and uracil repair by a family of DNA polymerases from phages with T-modified genomes
candidates.content: Abstract Replicative DNA polymerases (DNAPs) play a critical role in genome duplication, ensuring the accurate transmission of genetic information in all domains of life. DNAPs are also essential for DNA viruses, as well as bacteriophages, where a uracil-DNA glycosylase (UDG) is often encoded in trans or is present in the DNAP gene. Here, we identify a new group of A-family DNAPs in phages that are fused to an active UDG domain and contain other large insertions. Several members of this subfamily, including phages SP-15 and YerA41, are known to be hypermodified on their thymidine base through glycosylation of a linker attached to the C5 position of thymine. We determined the atomic cryo-EM structures for two of its members in various active functional and conformational states, from YerA41 and phiLo phages. The structures reveal how these large DNAPs function as replicative DNAPs, and how they can recognize dU bases ahead of the replication fork through their UDG domain, generating abasic sites that are preferentially bypassed through dA incorporation. Such dU errors would need to be eliminated to preserve phage genome integrity. Additionally, we report the co-occurrence of both an

candidates.title: Neuronal DNA repair mediates systemic mitochondrial maintenance through acetylcholine signaling
candidates.content: Abstract DNA repair defects such as nucleotide excision repair (NER) mutations can lead to progeroid syndromes characterized by growth retardation and accelerated aging with distinct tissue type specific pathologies. DNA-damage-induced dysfunction of specific cell types can impair the organism’s overall function. It is unknown whether, in reverse, DNA repair in specific tissues can have non-cell-autonomous consequences on other tissues carrying DNA damage. To explore the organismal consequences of cell-type-specific DNA repair, we restricted NER activity to specific tissues and monitored consequences on organismal health in Caenorhabditis elegans . Unexpectedly, we observed that tissue-specific DNA repair is sufficient to improve overall DNA damage resistance. Strikingly, NER activity restricted to neurons only is sufficient to provide similar overall DNA damage resistance as whole-body NER in almost all tissues tested. We show that this systemic DNA damage resilience is mediated by neuronal acetylcholine signaling that promotes the maintenance of mitochondrial activity throughout the organism.

candidates.title: Polymorphic Structures of an Artificial Nucleocapsid Evolved from a Circularly Permuted Bacterial Protein Cage
candidates.content: Molecular self-assembly provides a route to nanoscale structures with defined sizes and shapes. Protein cages assembled from repeated subunits form compartments that can package molecular cargoes. Although amino acid substitutions can alter intersubunit interactions and cage architecture, how protein backbone connectivity relates to the cage architectures accessible during laboratory evolution remains unclear. Here we evolved an artificial nucleocapsid from a circularly permuted variant of Aquifex aeolicus lumazine synthase (AaLS). Laboratory evolution increased the yield of purified nucleocapsids relative to the progenitor, and the evolved variant, NC119-3, packaged its encoding mRNA. Cryo-electron microscopy revealed a heterogeneous population of cages, within which we resolved 180- and 210-subunit cage families composed of 36 and 42 pentamers, respectively. Within each resolved family, particles with the same subunit stoichiometry differed in the arrangement and orientation of their pentameric building blocks. candidates.content: arXiv:2610.31673v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Forecasting pandemic spread across heterogeneous regions demands models that are both accurate and interpretable for public health action. This paper proposes a hybrid forecasting framework that integrates an SEIR epidemiological model enhanced with a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) to produce interpretable multi-horizon infection forecasts. Using region-wise COVID-19 data from the Our World in Data corpus, we present a unified pipeline that integrates epidemiological indicators (susceptible, exposed, infectious, recovered), intervention signals (masking, vaccination, policies), mobility covariates, and demographic context. The SEIR component estimates latent disease dynamics and injects mechanistic priors, while the TFT learns non-linear temporal dependencies and cross-feature interactions from historical observations and known future inputs. To ensure transparency, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) is applied at both global and local levels, quantifying feature contributions and revealing region-specific drivers of surges and slowdowns. candidates.title: Decoupling candidate dual AGN from chance superpositions in the GOTHIC survey via a deep-learning framework
candidates.content: arXiv:2608.24164v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Dual active galactic nuclei (DAGN) mark a critical phase in the evolution of merging galaxies and the pairing of supermassive black holes, yet they remain difficult to identify in large imaging surveys because of projection effects and limited spatial resolution. Compact foreground stars and unresolved substructure can mimic dual nuclei through chance superposition, complicating automated detection. We revisit the 46,061 galaxies flagged but rejected as DAGN candidates by the GOTHIC pipeline, primarily because the two nuclei fell within the SDSS fibre aperture or exceeded its separation threshold. We train a supervised deep-learning framework based on the YOLOv11 oriented-bounding-box architecture on annotated SDSS imaging to separate genuine dual nuclei from foreground stellar contaminants and other spurious alignments. candidates.title: JockeyBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Horse-Racing Decision-Making
candidates.content: Repeated event forecasting requires extracting predictive signals from noisy evidence and evaluating their value across successive decisions. We introduce JockeyBench, a benchmark and evaluation protocol that studies this problem through historical Japanese horse racing. The protocol combines time-gated evidence, priced tools, paired frozen-program controls, and two workflows: executing an LLM-written predictor or acquiring evidence for a fresh per-race LLM forecast. Evaluation separates forecast quality, benchmark-specific net utility, and retrospective betting returns and risk under fixed decision rules. Across 28 model--scaffold configurations on 324 races, paired tests identify seven revision gains and two declines after multiple-testing correction. Yet every configuration has negative mean profit under capped-Kelly settlement. In a four-model comparison, the reusable-program workflow has higher mean betting profit and lower research fees, although both workflows lose on average. Further diagnostics reveal that mean probability bias reverses on selected bets and that profitable individual runs can depend on concentrated returns. candidates.title: Profile-Driven User Simulation via Reinforcement Learning with Hierarchical Rewards for Task-Oriented Dialogues
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.32435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building Task-Oriented Dialogue (TOD) systems for high-value scenarios such as financial marketing requires large volumes of domain-specific dialogue data, which privacy regulations, annotation costs, and the need for expert labor make hard to obtain. User simulation offers a remedy, but existing methods target general-domain dialogue and exhibit two key limitations: insufficient modeling of domain-specific business processes and compliance constraints, and inadequate capture of the colloquial, spoken-language character of voice interactions. We propose ProfileSim, a profile-driven user simulation framework for financial marketing outbound calls. It jointly models user profiles---demographics and Big Five personality traits---and business profiles---intents reverse-engineered from real call logs---enabling fine-grained control over simulated behavior. candidates.content: arXiv:2610.32802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On-policy distillation aligns teacher feedback with a student's current behavior, yet acquiring useful supervision for multi-turn agents requires identifying both where guidance is needed and whether the student can sustain the interaction afterward. We introduce Frontier-OPD, which addresses this problem through the student's learning frontier: decision situations that remain challenging but admit useful autonomous continuation after brief teacher guidance. To operationalize this frontier, Frontier-OPD organizes on-policy experience into a shared-state trajectory graph, where trajectory-balanced aggregation of teacher-student disagreement identifies distinct intervention candidates while preserving the histories needed for replay. Short teacher bridges are then assessed by comparing agreement over the bridge and the ensuing student continuation with an equally long segment of the original trajectory, providing a behavioral proxy for guidance that the current student can build on. candidates.content: arXiv:2610.32638v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM inference is increasingly deployed as a core service for enterprise and interactive applications, but sovereignty, compliance, latency and resource-locality requirements can limit the suitability of centralised cloud deployments. Telco operators offer geographically distributed compute and network infrastructure for addressing these constraints. However, existing LLM serving frameworks are designed for tightly coupled data centres and provide limited support for coordinating geographically distributed and heterogeneous resources. We present InferSlice, a reference architecture for Service-Level Objective (SLO)-driven LLM inference over a telco infrastructure, integrating network slicing, GPU partitioning, elastic serving and observability. candidates.content: arXiv:2609.05279v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multiagent LLM systems often treat a role as a slot: when a member is replaced, any agent competent at the role is expected to fill it. We test this view on teams whose members keep short written notebooks. A one-seat swap replays a formed, frozen team with its own member, with a same-role newcomer carrying another team's notebook for that role, or with a newcomer carrying none. In cooperative cooking, wildfire response and medical question answering, the experienced newcomer, averaged over seats, outscores the one without a notebook in every setting, so the usual comparison would approve it. Against the original team, the same replacement falls short in every setting, and the team spends more messages per unit of progress. candidates.title: From Review to Authorization: Key-Isolated Threshold Signing for LLM Agents
candidates.content: arXiv:2609.05901v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Autonomous LLM agents can turn semantic judgments into consequential actions such as payments and permission changes. If the same process makes these judgments and controls a reusable signing credential, a mistaken judgment can reach execution without further approval. To make LLM review govern execution, we present KITA, an authorization architecture that keeps the user's personal signing key and every threshold signing-key share outside all LLM processes. Under threshold-signature unforgeability and our system assumptions, an adversary controlling the proposer and fewer than t reviewer-signer domains cannot produce a valid authorization for a new action without signing contributions from t distinct domains. This execution-bound authorization integrity ensures that each accepted authorization includes a share from an uncompromised domain, bound to the canonical action and released only after authenticated reviewer approval. We implement an in-process prototype of KITA with a structured-output LLM adapter and threshold BLS. candidates.content: arXiv:2610.27746v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Simulating economic responses at society scale requires agents whose decisions reflect household circumstances. We introduce S$^2$-MAS, a society-scale multi-agent simulation framework built on 500 million synthetic household personas grounded in real-survey data. Its Genese engine separates decisions from state updates, while reusable financial scenarios and application ledgers track consumption, cash, debt and payments. Trained with SFT + RLCD on 2.93 million examples, sharp-421m-mlx achieves 74.55% accuracy and 38.37% question-macro F1 on one-shot consumer financial-choice tasks derived from held-out survey responses. Its accuracy exceeds GLM-5.3-Flash, Jev 1.13, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GPT-6-Luna and GPT-6-Astra in the common benchmark (full test for the first four; matched 500-group sample for Astra). We evaluate eight financial task families and simulate 12 million distinct household agents in paired purchase-funding conditions. candidates.title: Towards Adversarially Robust Multigraph Neural Networks for Financial Crime Analysis
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.31718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Financial transaction networks are naturally represented as multigraphs, where repeated transactions between the same pair of accounts are modeled as distinct edges. Recently proposed multigraph neural network architectures leverage this structure explicitly to achieve a strong performance on anti-money laundering (AML) tasks. However, their robustness to adversaries that manipulate transaction structures to evade detection remains largely unexplored. We present the first scalable framework for structural attacks and adversarial training of multigraph neural networks using node-edge incidence matrices, adapting projected gradient descent and projected randomized block coordinate descent methods to optimize structural perturbations over such matrices. We further introduce a cycle-based regularizer that penalizes changes in the global counts of directed 2- and 3-cycles, providing a structural measure of attack plausibility.
